entry.name: pattrstorage
entry.description: View and modify client object data, and store or recall presets.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: A symbol argument may be optionally used to set theobject's scripting name. In the absence of an argument, theobject is given an arbitrary, semi-random name, such as u197000004.

attributes.name: activewritemode
attributes.digest: Write mode of active property
attributes.description: Sets the write mode for theproperty of client objects. The default is 0 (disabled). When enabled, the active state of client objects will be saved with the XML preset data file and restored when this file is re-read.

attributes.name: annotation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: annotation_name
attributes.digest: Info View Title

attributes.name: autopattr_vis
attributes.digest: Autopattr visibility
attributes.description: Sets the visibility ofobjects in the clientwindow and storagewindow displays. The default is 0 (disabled). Sinceobjects are not used for forming path names, one can generally ignore them for the purposes of display. When performingobject functions, such as setting thestate orfor an entire set of objects being exposed by a singleobject, the user needs to know the name of the objects' actual container object. Enablingmay make this process somewhat clearer visually and conceptually.

attributes.name: autorestore
attributes.digest: Autorestore state
attributes.description: Enables or disables theobject's autorestore state. The default is 1 (on). When enabled, theobject will automatically try to locate and read an XML file representing preset data when the patcher loads. Theobject will attempt to load the last-saved file. If theobject in question has never saved a file, the object will attempt to load a file with the name (name).xml, where (name) is the patcher name of theobject (usually, its argument).

attributes.name: autowatch
attributes.digest: File-watch state
attributes.description: Sets theobject's file watching behavior. The default is 0 (disabled). When file watching is enabled, the most recently read or written XML data file will be reloaded automatically if it is modified. This allows you to use an external editor for your XML data file. When you save the file, theobject will notice. Note that when the file is re-read, any currently unsaved data will be lost.

attributes.name: background
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: backupmode
attributes.digest: Number of backup XML files
attributes.description: Sets the number of backup XML files to be maintained and rotated by theobject when writing files. The default is 0 (disabled). The argument specifies the number of backups theobject should make before the files start rotating (being automatically deleted to make room for new backups). The most recent backup is called pstoname.bak.xml. The next, pstoname_1.bak.xml, followed by pstoname_2.bak.xml, etc.

attributes.name: changemode
attributes.digest: Change mode behavior
attributes.description: Sets theobject's data-filtration behavior. The default is 0 (disabled). When enabled, only changed values are sent from theobject to client objects, and repeated data is filtered.

attributes.name: client_rect
attributes.digest: Client list window location and size
attributes.description: Sets a new size and position for the client list window. The window position is specified in global coordinates by 4 numbers (left, top, right, bottom).

attributes.name: color
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: dirty
attributes.digest: Patcher dirty flag
attributes.description: Enables or disables the patcher-dirty flag. The default is 0 (disabled). When enabled, theobject will dirty the patch whenever its state changes.

attributes.name: fileusagemode
attributes.digest: File storage in collectives and standalones
attributes.description: Enables or disables the inclusion of JSON/XML storage files in collectives and standalones. The default is 0 (include storage file).

attributes.name: flat
attributes.digest: Client list display format
attributes.description: Enables or disables theobject's client list display flag. The default is 0 (disabled). When enabled, theobject's 2 windows will not display a hierarchical view of clients, instead display only data-containing objects (no patchers), and their full path name or alias.

attributes.name: fontface
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: fontname
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: fontsize
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: greedy
attributes.digest: Child patcher access flag
attributes.description: Sets theobject's client search behavior flag. Theattribute provides a way to limit the amount of data a singleobject will manage. The following values are possible:0 = disabled (the default). Theobject can see allobjects or objects bound toobjects in any child patches of theobject (or child patches of those child patches, tunneling down through the patcher hierarchy), until anotherobject is found. Although theobject found in a child patch will be a client of the parentobject, no other objects at that level or below in the patcher hierarchy will be.1 = see everything. When theattribute is set to 1, theobject can see everything, all the way down to the bottom of the patcher hierarchy (including anyobjects it finds along the way).2 = clients only. When theattribute is set to 2, theobject can only see potential client objects in its patch. No other patches are searched.

attributes.name: hidden
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: hint
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: ignoreclick
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: jspainterfile
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: notifymode
attributes.digest: Notification behavior
attributes.description: Sets theobject's add/remove-notification behavior. The default is 0 (disabled). When enabled, theobject will send a message from it's outlet every time an object is added or removed from its client list, in the form. Note that theobject must occasionally purge and fully rebuild its client list in response to certain events, resulting in significant output whenis enabled and objects are being added and removed regularly.

attributes.name: outputmode
attributes.digest: Auto-output behavior
attributes.description: Sets theobject's auto-output behavior. The default is 0 (disabled). When enabled, theobject will send a message from its outlet every time a value is sent to one of its client objects, in the form. The following modes are available:0 = disabled1 = output all values sent to client objects2 = output only changed values sent to client objects (see)3 = output all values sent to client objects not initiated by a message to theobject4 = output only changed values sent to client objects not initiated by a message to theobject (see)5 = output all values sent to client objects not initiated by a message to any-system object (,,,).6 = output only changed values sent to client objects not initiated by a message to any-system object (see)

attributes.name: parameter_enable
attributes.digest: Enable parameter mode
attributes.description: Enables use of this object withandin Max..

attributes.name: patching_rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: position
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: presentation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: presentation_rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: savemode
attributes.digest: Sets theobject's save behavior.
attributes.description: Sets theobject's save behavior. The default is 1 (prompt on object free). In this mode, if theobject's preset data has changed (presets have been stored, deleted or modified since the last fileoroperation) at the time the object is freed, the object will prompt the user to write a preset file. In mode 2,will attempt to autosave a preset file (without user interaction), whenever the patcher is saved. In mode 0, pattrstorage will neither prompt nor autosave. In mode 3,will attempt to autosave a preset file (without user interaction), whenever the patcher is freed.The following values are possible:0 = Neither prompt nor autosave1 = Prompt the user to save a preset file when the object is freed (default)2 = Attempt to autosave whenever the patcher is saved, or if unsuccessful, prompt the user to save a preset file3 = Attempt to autosave (without user interaction) when the patcher is freed. Failing that, prompt the user

attributes.name: size
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: storage_rect
attributes.digest: Stored data window size and location
attributes.description: Sets a new size and position for the stored data window. The window position is specified in global coordinates by 4 numbers (left, top, right, bottom).

attributes.name: subscribemode
attributes.digest: Subscription mode
attributes.description: Sets the subscription mode. The default is 0 (disabled). When enabled, theobject uses a user-specified subscription list to determine which objects are clients, rather than discovering and maintaining all objects within the patcher/patcher hierarchy (as determined by theattribute. Theandmessages can be used to add and remove objects to and from this list, and themessage can be used to output a list of currently subscribed objects.

attributes.name: textcolor
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: textjustification
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: varname
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: writefilter
attributes.digest: Filter Missing Objects' Data on Write
attributes.description: When enabled (default), missing objects' data will be excluded from preset files saved by theobject. When disabled, the data will be retained.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: Double-clicking on aobject opens the object's client list window, as if the object had received themessage.

messages.name: active
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies the path name or alias of a client object and a 1 or 0, sets that object's active status. When a client object is active (default), its data will be recalled when presets are recalled--otherwise, the object is ignored during recall. Setting thestate of a parent object (such as a patcher-any client object containing other client objects), automatically sets thestate of the child objects of the parent to the same value.

messages.name: alias
messages.digest: Create an alias for a client
messages.description: The word, followed by two symbols, generates an alias for the client object whose path name is given in the first argument. The alias permits the object to be referred to by a name given in the second argument.For example,would alias the object at the location a_patcher::a_pattr to the name the_pattr.Aliases can be used interchangeably with path names within theobject, and are useful for referring to long paths by simpler, shorter names.getThe word get, followed by a symbol that specifies the path name of a client object, returns that object's alias (if any) from theobject's outlet, preceded by the symbol.

messages.name: anything
messages.description: Incoming messages to theobject are analyzed. If the first element of the message matches the path name or alias of an object maintained by theobject (visible in the object's client list), the subsequent arguments in the message set that object's value. Otherwise, the message is ignored.

messages.name: clear
messages.description: The wordremoves all presets from theobject's internal list.

messages.name: client_close
messages.description: Closes the client list window.

messages.name: clientwindow
messages.description: Opens theobject's client list window (the title bar reads clientwindow (name), where (name) is the patcher name of the pattrstorage object which created the window).

messages.name: copy
messages.description: The word, followed by 2 or 3 arguments, copies the stored values from one numbered preset to another. Followed by 2 numbers, the stored values from the preset slot specified by the first number will be copied to the preset slot specified by the second number. If that slot doesn't yet exist, it will be automatically created. Followed by a symbol and 2 numbers, the stored values from a preset slot, as specified by the first number, of theobject referred to by the symbol will be copied to a preset slot, as specified by the second number, of the object receiving themessage. For example, the messagewould cause preset 3 of theobject called psto_parent, located in the parent patch of theobject receiving themessage, to be copied to preset 1 of theobject receiving the message. In order for this to function reliably, client path names must match exactly. If they do not, the data for that client is ignored.

messages.name: delete
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, clears any data in the preset whose index is specified by that number and removes the preset from theobject's internal list. Ifis not followed by an argument, all presets are cleared and removed. See themessage for further information on viewing the object's list of presets.

messages.name: dump
messages.description: The wordreports the current value of all client objects from theobject's outlet as a series of messages, each in the form. The output ofis finished when the messageis output.

messages.name: fade
messages.description: Identical to themessage. Deprecated.

messages.name: fillempty
messages.description: The wordsets the value of any empty preset slots for all client objects to the current value of the respective object. For clientobjects with anvalue, the initial value will be used instead. No data is sent to the client objects themselves.

messages.name: float
messages.description: Recalls the data from the preset specified by. If the number falls between two whole numbers (e.g.), theobject will interpolate between the data stored in the preset corresponding to the integer portion of the float and the data stored at the preset numbered one higher (e.g.will causeto interpolate 50% between presets 1 and 2). See themessage for more information about interpolation modes.

messages.name: getactive
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies the path name or alias of a client object, reports the active status of the client object from theobject's outlet, preceded by the symbol.

messages.name: getalias
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies the path name or alias of a client object, will causeto return that client-object's alias from its outlet.

messages.name: getclientlist
messages.digest: Output a list of pattr clients
messages.description: The wordreports the path names of any client objects from theobject's outlet as a series of messages, each preceded by the symbol. The output ofis finished when the messageis output.

messages.name: getcurrent
messages.description: The wordreports the currently active preset from theobject's outlet, preceded by the symbol.

messages.name: getedited
messages.description: The wordreports the edit state of the currently active preset from theobject's outlet, preceded by the symbol. If the data in the currently active preset has been edited, the state is reported as. Otherwise, the edit state is reported as.

messages.name: getinterp
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies the path name or alias of a client object, reports that object's interpolation mode from theobject's outlet, preceded by the symbol.

messages.name: getlockedslots
messages.digest: Output a list of locked presets
messages.description: The wordreports the indices of any locked slots from theobject's outlet as a list, preceded by the symbol.

messages.name: getpriority
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies the path name or alias of a client object, reports that object's priority from theobject's outlet, preceded by the symbol.

messages.name: getslotlist
messages.digest: Output a list of available presets
messages.description: The wordreports the numbers of any valid presets from theobject's outlet, preceded by the symbol.

messages.name: getslotname
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, causes the name of the preset slot specified by the number to be output from the pattrstorage object's outlet, preceded by the symbol.

messages.name: getslotnamelist
messages.digest: Output a list of preset names
messages.description: The word, followed by an optional number, reports the slot names of all used slots to be sent from theobject's outlet as a series of messages, each preceded by the symbol. The output ofis finished when the messageis output.Without an argument, or with an argument of 0, themessage will cause all slots from 0 to the largest stored slot number to be output, regardless of whether the slot has been defined or not. This facilitates the use of themessage with objects such as. To filter undefined slots (even if they have names), send themessage with a non-0 argument.For more information, see theobject's help file.

messages.name: getstoredvalue
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies the path name or alias of a client object and a number which specifies a preset, reports that object's value, as stored in that preset slot, from theobject's outlet, in the form.

messages.name: getsubscriptionlist
messages.digest: Output a list of subscribed items
messages.description: The wordcauses the names of all subscribed objects to be sent from theobject's outlet as a series of messages, each preceded by the symbol. The output ofis finished when the messageis output. See theattribute for more information.

messages.name: grab
messages.description: The wordcauses the current value of all client objects to be reacquired by theobject. This is particularly useful when theobject is managing client objects whose data changes internally, without sending notifications to thesystem.

messages.name: insert
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, stores the data for every object maintained byin a numbered preset. The number argument specifies the index of the preset to be stored. Any presets numbers at the specified index or higher are automatically incremented to make room for the inserted preset.

messages.name: int
messages.description: Recalls the data from the preset specified by.

messages.name: interp
messages.description: The word, followed by at least 1 and up to 3 arguments (,,), sets the interpolation status and mode for a specific client object. The first symbol specifies the path name or alias of a client object. The second symbol argument determines the mode, and can be one of the following values:- No interpolation. Same as no additional argument.- Linear interpolation. Presets recalled usingormessages will be interpolated using a standard linear algorithm.- Threshold. Takes optional 3rd argument, which sets the threshold. Presets recalled usingormessages will recall data from the first preset specified when the fade amount is below the threshold, and will recall data from the second preset specified when the fade amount is greater than or equal to the threshold.- Inverse threshold. Takes optional 3rd argument (), which sets the threshold. Presets recalled usingormessages will recall data from the first preset specified when the fade amount is greater than or equal to the threshold, and will recall data from the second preset specified when the fade amount is less than the threshold.- Power curve. Takes optional 3rd argument (), which sets the exponent to which the fade amount will be raised. Presets recalled usingormessages will recall data between the two specified presets, along the curve described. Power curves can be used to create faster or slower "attacks" and "decays" for the fade envelope.- Table-specified curve. Takes optional 3rd argument (), which specifies the name of a table to use for curve lookup. Presets recalled usingormessages will recall data between the two specified presets, along the curve described in the table. Tables are assumed to contain values between 0 and 100, representing the new fade amount * 100 (this is clipped internal to theobject, but is not normalized). The length of the table is stretched to match the expected fade values (between 0 and 1), so any number of table entries can be used. If the lookup fade amount does not fall exactly onto a table-specified value, linear interpolation is used to determine the new fade amount. Please see thehelp file for examples of table-specified interpolation.

messages.name: locate
messages.digest: Open the patcher containing an object
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol corresponding to the path name or alias of an object, will cause the containing patcher of that object to be opened.

messages.name: lock
messages.digest: Set the lock status of a preset
messages.description: The word, followed by 2 numbers, sets the lock status for a particular preset number. The first argument specifies the preset number to be locked or unlocked. The second argument specifies the lock state, and should be either 0 (unlocked) or 1 (locked). Locked presets cannot be deleted (using theormessages) or overwritten (using themessage). Locked presets can be moved (as a result of,ormessages, if performed on other presets). Locks are saved in the preset data file.

messages.name: lockall
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the lock status for all presets at once. The argument specifies the lock state, and should be either 0 (unlocked) or 1 (locked). Locked presets cannot be deleted (using theormessages) or overwritten (using themessage). Locked presets can be moved (as a result of,ormessages, if performed on other, unlocked presets). Locks are saved in the preset data file.

messages.name: priority
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies the path name or alias of a client object and a number, sets the recall and display priority for that object. When presets are recalled, the data for client objects will be restored in the order established by. Lower priorities are executed first. Negative priorities are permitted. Priority is only respected within a single level of the patcher hierarchy. Data in parent patchers will always be restored before data in nested patchers.

messages.name: purge
messages.description: The wordrebuilds the internal client list of theobject, removing entries for client objects which have been deleted or moved. Typically, theobject retains a reference to such objects, so that their settings (,,, etc.) can be restored if the objects reappear.

messages.name: read
messages.description: The word, followed by an optional symbol that specifies a filename, reads an JSON or XML file representing preset data from disk into theobject. If the argument is given, and represents a valid file path, the file will be read from that location--otherwise, a standard File Dialog will be presented for the user to manually choose the file to be read.

messages.name: readagain
messages.description: The wordre-reads an JSON or XML file previously specified by theormessages. If no file has been previously specified, a standard File Dialog will be presented for the user to manually choose the file to be read.

messages.name: recall
messages.description: The word, followed by 1 to 4 arguments, recalls data from a preset. Ifis followed by a number or a floating-point number, the data for every object whose value is stored in the specified preset (or in the interpolated preset represented by a floating-point number - see themessage) will be recalled. Ifis followed by 2 arguments--a symbol and a number--and theargument matches the path name or alias of a client object, only the data for the specified object will be recalled. The number argument always specifies the index (or interpolated index) of the preset to recall.Followed by 3 or 4 arguments, themessage recalls interpolated data from 2 presets at a specified weight between the two. If the wordis followed by two numbers that specify the indices of two presets and a a floating point number between 0 and 1.0 that specifies an interpolation value, the data for every object whose value is stored in the specified presets will be recalled.Ifis followed by a symbol that specifies the path name or alias of a client object followed by two numbers that specify the indices of two presets and a floating point interpolation value, only the data for the specified object will be recalled.In these latter cases, the floating point argument specifies the weight of the interpolation, and should be between 0. and 1. A floating point argument ofwould simply recall the data for the preset matching the first index, andwould recall the data for the preset matching the second index. See themessage for more information about interpolation modes.

messages.name: recallmulti
messages.digest: The word, followed by at least 2 numeric arguments, permits weighted recall of multiple presets.
messages.description: The word, followed by at least 2 numeric arguments, permits weighted recall of multiple presets. Each argument determines the (normalized) weight of a particular preset in the final output. If the argument is an integer, the weight is 100%. If the argument is a floating point number, the integer part of the number determines the preset number, and the floating point part of the number determines the weight. For instance,would weight preset 1 at 30%, preset 2 at 30% and preset 5 at 40%. Since weights are normalized, the total weight can be higher than 100%; for instance,would calculate correct weights (27.77%, 27.77% and 44.44% respectively), and,andall result in the same output (33.33% for each member).

messages.name: remove
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, deletes the data for every object maintained byin a numbered preset. The number argument specifies the index of the preset to be removed. Any presets numbers higher than the specified index are automatically decremented.

messages.name: renumber
messages.description: The wordrenumbers stored presets into consecutive preset slots, beginning with slot 1.

messages.name: resolvealias
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies the alias of a client object, returns that object's full path name (if any) from theobject's outlet, preceded by the symbol.

messages.name: setall
messages.digest: Set a value for all presets
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies the path name or alias of a client object and a variable number of additional arguments corresponding to the value of the client object, sets the value of the specified client objectto that value. No data is sent to the client object itself.

messages.name: setstoredvalue
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies the path name or alias of a client object, a number which specifies a preset and a variable number of additional arguments corresponding to the data expected by the client object, sets the value of the specified client object within the specified preset slot to the specified data.

messages.name: slotname
messages.digest: Provide a name for a preset
messages.description: The word, followed by a number and an optional symbol, sets the name of the preset slot specified by the number. If the symbol argument is not present, the name of the slot is removed. Undefined slots can be given names for labeling purposes. If aobject is linked to theobject, it will display the slot name of the correspondingslot.

messages.name: storage_close
messages.description: Closes the stored data window.

messages.name: storagewindow
messages.description: Opens theobject's stored data window (the title bar reads storagewindow (name), where (name) is the patcher name of the pattrstorage object which created the window).

messages.name: store
messages.description: The word, followed by 1 or 2 arguments, stores data in a numbered preset. If the wordis followed by a number, the data for every object maintained bywill be stored. Ifis followed by 2 arguments--a symbol and a number--and the symbol argument matches the path name or alias of a client object, only the data for the specified object will be stored. The number argument always specifies the index of the preset to be stored. If the preset index specified by the number argument is already in use, the existing data will be overwritten without a warning.A storage slot of '0' is allowed, but *IS NOT SAVED* in a file. It can be used as a temporary slot for interpolation activities or other non-permanent experiments.

messages.name: storeagain
messages.digest: Store a preset in the last-used slot
messages.description: The wordsimply executes aoperation, using the most recently-use preset slot. If there is no previously-used preset slot (if themessage has never been sent to the object), the message is ignored.

messages.name: storenext
messages.digest: Store a present in an empty slot
messages.description: The wordexecutes aoperation, using the next empty preset slot, counting up from preset 1. For instance, if preset slots 1, 2 and 4 have data stored in them, and theobject receives themessage, the current state of the client objects would be stored to preset slot 3. A secondmessage would cause the data to be stored to preset slot 5.

messages.name: subscribe
messages.digest: Add clients to the subscription list
messages.description: The word, followed by one or more symbols, each corresponding to the path name or alias of an object, will add the specified object to theobject's subscription list. See theattribute for more information.

messages.name: unsubscribe
messages.digest: Remove clients from the subscription list
messages.description: The word, followed by one or more symbols, each corresponding to the path name or alias of an object, will remove the specified object from theobject's subscription list. See theattribute for more information.

messages.name: write
messages.description: The word, followed by an optional symbol that specifies a filename, writes any preset data to a JSON file on disk. If the argument is given, and represents a valid file path, the file will be saved at that location - otherwise, a standard File Dialog will be presented for the user to manually choose a name and location for the file to be saved.

messages.name: writeagain
messages.description: The wordwrites any preset data to a JSON file on disk previously specified by theormessages. If no file has been previously specified, a standard File Dialog will be presented for the user to manually choose a name and location for the file to be saved.

messages.name: writejson
messages.digest: Write presets as a JSON file
messages.description: The word, followed by an optional symbol that specifies a filename, writes any preset data to a file on disk, in JSON format. If the argument is given, and represents a valid file path, the file will be saved at that location--otherwise, a standard File Dialog will be presented for the user to manually choose a name and location for the file to be saved.

messages.name: writexml
messages.digest: Write presets as an XML file
messages.description: The word, followed by an optional symbol that specifies a filename, writes any preset data to a file on disk, in XML format. If the argument is given, and represents a valid file path, the file will be saved at that location--otherwise, a standard File Dialog will be presented for the user to manually choose a name and location for the file to be saved.
